## QUESTION

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).


To seperate data in order to find the factors I wanted I first seperated based on whether or not a house was built before or during/after 1980. Early test I ran showed there were no null values in the yrbuilt column and no weird outliers to I'm confindent that there won't be skewing of my data. 

After seperating the data I looked at the medians and averages for each value to get an idea of the biggest differences.

I settled on:

livearea: homes from 1980 and onward have around 600 more sqft of livable space on average

arcstyle_ONE-STORY: only 6.4% of houses from 1980 and onward have a one story architectural style whereas 56.3% of houses from before 1980 have an one story architectural style.

tasp: the average tax assesed selling price for a 1980 and onward home is around $100,000 more than a house from before 1980.

These differences seemed the most significant and I think using these in combination with each other and other potential factors will help me to have a high success rate.

1. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).  

Despite the factors I guessed on before the reality was that no single column had a major impact how what distinguished a home as being built before 1980 or during/after. Because of this I decided to use a RandomForestClassifier ML Model. It's use of averaging to decided the best way to distinguish and find important factors has created a consistent 92%-93% accuracy on all tests I've run. I decided to go with 400 estimators just to make sure I run enough tests though accurary showed litte difference from 100 to 400. I also used -1 for the n_jobs to allow the program to use my cores in parallel to speed up calculations. 

I decided on a 20/80 split so the ML model had plenty to train off of and therefore would have better averages.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
# Don't forget, you need another import statement to import the desired ML model from sklearn

y = (data["yrbuilt"] < 1980).to_numpy()
X = data.drop("yrbuilt", "before1980", "parcel", strict=False)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42
)

model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=400, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("forest", accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test)))
```
